recipes.name: Irish Cream Bundt Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan with cooking spray. Sprinkle chopped nuts evenly over the bottom of the pan.
Combine cake mix and pudding mix in a large bowl. Beat in eggs, Irish cream liqueur, oil, and water with an electric mixer on high speed for 5 minutes. Pour batter over nuts in the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of cake comes out clean, about 1 hour. Let cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes.

While cake is cooling, make glaze: Combine sugar, butter, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil and continue boiling for 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and stir in Irish cream.
Invert cake onto a serving dish. Prick the top and sides of cake with a toothpick. Spoon glaze over the top and brush onto the sides. Allow cake to absorb glaze, then repeat until glaze is used up.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Cream Bundt Cake
raw_recipe.description: This Baileys Irish cream cake is baked with box mix and instant pudding, then glazed with more liqueur for a moist and delicious pecan-topped Bundt.

review.reviewBody:
Great cake!. I have had many repeat requests every time I take it somewhere. 
I handle the glaze differently than the recipe with much better results.
After I remove the cake and let it cool 20 minutes, I poke holes in the cake, make the glaze, then pour the glaze into the bundt pan and replace the cake in the pan. I let it sit another 20 minutes and then turn it out onto a cake round. All the glaze is absorbed and it gives a pretty finish to the crust. Then I sprinkle a few more finely chopped pecans over the top for presentation.

I loved this! So moist!! I forgot to read reviews until it was in the oven. So here’s what I did to make it moist and tasty: I soaked the pecans in some Irish cream for a while, and then drained them before putting them in the bottom of my Bundt pan that had been buttered and sugared. Then after 10 minutes out of the oven, I poked holes in the cake and poured half of the glaze in it before turning it over on a platter. I tried to poke holes again but it was so tender it was almost falling apart. So I just poured the rest of the glaze all over and brushed it on the sides and the inside also! Absolutely delicious! Gone instantly at a luncheon I took it to. Will make again!

I made the cake following the recipe and suggestions from previous bakers: I used 1 C Baileys in the cake instead of 3/4 C and 1/4 C water, I used a Duncan Hines cake mix and I poured 2/3 of the glaze into the pan and put the warm cake back in to absorb it. 
I brought this cake to a party last night and it was a hit. It was super moist with a nice crust on the outside and the Baileys flavor was smooth and perfect (I used real Baileys because it is so much better than the other options as it contains whiskey and not wine) I had to save a piece to bring home for my daughter who was begging to have some the whole time it cooked- it made the house smell amazing! My friend, who is a caterer, told me it was a top 10 cake she has had. I will definitely be baking it again. Love it!

Usually make this with yellow cake mix and vanilla pudding, but we’re going to mix things up and use choc cake/choc pudding. I like my boozy cake so saturated that I shouldn’t walk near an open flame after eating it—we’re a bit more generous with the Irish creme in the glaze. 😉 And flip the cake upside down in the Bundt pan before poking holes in it so that the top will really soak up that glaze. And we use a chopstick instead of a toothpick to get the glaze all the way thru.
This was good. Used 1 C Irish Cream, rather than 3/4 C plus 1/4 C water. Also followed other recommendations to put glaze in pan, then put cake back in to absorb.

I always come back to this recipe. I skipped the nuts, used the full cup of Bailey's Irish Cream and skipped the water in the batter, and added 2 dashes of nutmeg more so for the specs that you see as opposed to for taste. Bought the Pam baking with flour spray for the bundt pan and it was a game changer! This is not an ad lol

Great cake! I omitted the nuts and changed the sugar in the glaze to dark brown sugar for a fuller flavour. I've also baked it in two separate 7.5 inch bundt pans for about 45 mins. Freezes well. Extra glaze can be warmed up and drizzled over the cake and /or ice cream too.

Very easy to make and has great flavor. I did add a little extra Bailey's to the glaze for a stronger flavor. 
I highly recommend once its cool, removing the cake from the pan and adding half the glaze to the bottom off the bundt pan. Poke some holes all around the cake then place it back into bundt pan and pour the rest of glaze over the bottom. It absorbs very quick and is nicely covered. 
Enjoy!!

Made this for our family cabin trip. Everyone Loved it! The kicker is I didn't even use Irish cream, however I did use Irish cream flavoring! For the cake I used yellow cake mix with pudding in it but I also used 1/2 the amount of pudding mix called for - in chocolate flavor - to give it a brownish color. I also threw in about 1 Tbsp. baking cocoa as well. Since I didn't put in the alcohol I used almond milk for the liquid. In the glaze I simply added the flavoring but no extra liquid along with the other ingredients. In both the cake and glaze I used about 2 tsp. flavoring each. Delicious! Will make again.
So moist and delicious! I use 1 cup of Irish cream instead of water. Comes out amazing every time. Always a hit at work.
Instead of using 1/4 c of wAter, I upped the Baileys to 1 cup. It was to die for!!!
I made this cake as per recipe. It was absolutely delicious!!! Will be making again.

Great recipe and easy to follow. This is the second time making it for St. Patrick's Day, but this time I used the suggestion to pour the glaze into the pan and place the cake on top of it for 20 minutes. That worked better than pouring it over the top.

Cake was ok, nothing special. I even added a whole cup of Irish cream like some suggested. The "glaze" ended up being super thick, more like icing. Couldn't even spread it on the cake. I've made many glazes before, not sure why this didn't work for me
Substituted salted caramel cream liquor for the Baileys--otherwise, everything was exactly the same. A huge hit--my family asks for this cake all the time!
Wonderful recipe... I used 1 cup of Irish Cream and no water in the batter. .. delicious. Same with the Glaze... will definitely be making it again.
this was amazing
Can use flavored coffee creamer instead of liqueur.

The recipe is perfect the way it is written. I did use brown sugar for the glaze instead of white, but that is all I altered. I would be very cautious about following some of the comments that are telling you to put the glaze in the bottom of the pan and put the cake back in to absorb the icing. I did not take that suggestion because I am not sure how you get the cake back out of the pan once the icing turns to carmel. I would imagine the cake will be stuck to the bottom of the pan. All that work for nothing.

My husband loved this! The house smelled wonderful while baking, so we knew it would taste as well as the aroma. We can't wait to try the same recipe, but with different flavors of cream liqueurs! definitely a keeper!
